title: 三相四线制中的 3 次谐波：中线电流
statement: 对称三相电源（正序）每相电动势含基波和 3 次谐波：u_A = 220√2 cos(314t) + 40√2 cos(942t) V，u_B、u_C 的基波依次滞后 120°，即 u_B = 220√2 cos(314t − 120°) + 40√2 cos(3(314t − 120°)) V，u_C 类推。
电源经三相四线制向对称星形负载供电，每相 R = 20 Ω、L = 15.92 mH（ωL = 5 Ω），中线阻抗为零，电流表 A_N 测中线电流。
求负载相电压（= 电源相电压）的有效值、线电压 U_AB 的有效值、A 相电流有效值和中线电流表的读数。

questions.ask: A 相电流有效值 I_A = ?

questions.explain: 三相基波电流对称，在中线中相加为零；3 次谐波电流同相，相加为 3I_A3 = 4.8 A。

questions.ask: 如果把相电压的有效值乘以 √3 当作线电压，会发生什么？
choices: 偏大：3 次谐波在线电压中互相抵消，不能乘 √3
偏小：漏掉了 3 次谐波的 √3 倍
结果正确：线电压总是相电压的 √3 倍
偏大：基波在线电压中会互相抵消
choiceExplain: 3 次谐波在线电压里是**相减**为零，而不是乘以 √3。
U_l = √3U_p 只对对称的正序（或负序）分量成立，零序的 3 次谐波不满足。
抵消的是同相位的 3 次谐波，不是彼此相差 120° 的基波。
questions.explain: √3 × 223.6 = 387.3 V > 381.1 V。线电压中只有基波（以及 5、7 次等非 3 倍数的谐波）满足 √3 关系，3 的倍数次谐波在线电压中消失。

hints: 先看 3 次谐波：把 u_B、u_C 的 3 次谐波展开，3 × 120° 是多少？三相的 3 次谐波之间是什么相位关系？
基波按对称三相电路计算（中线中没有基波电流）；3 次谐波三相同相，相当于三个相同的单相电路，电流都流入中线。
线电压是两相电压之差：同相的分量在相减时抵消。电流和电压的有效值仍是各次谐波的平方和开方。
solution: **1. 谐波的相序。** 基波是正序（A、B、C 依次差 120°）。三个 3 次谐波的初相都是 3 × (−120°) = −360° ≡ 0°（以及 3 × 120° ≡ 0°）：同相位，构成**零序**分量。
**检查：** 3 次谐波的中线电流可以看成一个单相回路：三相并联的负载 Z_3/3 接在 40 V 上，40/(25/3) = 4.8 A，一致。

en.title: 3rd harmonics in a four-wire three-phase system: the neutral current
statement: Each phase EMF of a balanced (positive-sequence) three-phase source contains a fundamental and a 3rd harmonic: u_A = 220√2 cos(314t) + 40√2 cos(942t) V; the fundamentals of u_B, u_C lag by 120° each, i.e. u_B = 220√2 cos(314t − 120°) + 40√2 cos(3(314t − 120°)) V, and so on for u_C.
The source feeds a balanced Y load over a four-wire system; each phase is R = 20 Ω with L = 15.92 mH (ωL = 5 Ω), the neutral has zero impedance and the ammeter A_N measures the neutral current.
Find the rms load phase voltage (= source phase voltage), the rms line voltage U_AB, the rms current of phase A and the neutral ammeter reading.
hints: Start with the 3rd harmonic: expand the 3rd harmonics of u_B and u_C — what is 3 × 120°? How are the three 3rd harmonics related in phase?

Treat the fundamental as a balanced three-phase circuit (no fundamental current in the neutral); the 3rd harmonics are in phase, like three identical single-phase circuits whose currents all return through the neutral.
A line voltage is the difference of two phase voltages: components that are in phase cancel. rms values are still the root of the sum of the squares of the harmonics.
solution: **1. Sequence of the harmonics.** The fundamental is positive sequence (A, B, C 120° apart). The three 3rd harmonics have initial phases 3 × (−120°) = −360° ≡ 0° (and 3 × 120° ≡ 0°): they are in phase — a **zero-sequence** set.
**2. Fundamental** (ωL = 5 Ω): Z_1 = 20 + j5 = 20.62∠14.04° Ω, I_A1 = 220/20.62 = 10.67 A; the three phases are balanced and the neutral carries no fundamental current.
**3. 3rd harmonic** (3ωL = 15 Ω): Z_3 = 20 + j15 = 25∠36.87° Ω, I_A3 = I_B3 = I_C3 = 40/25 = 1.6 A, all in phase; the neutral current is I_N = 3 × 1.6 = **4.8 A**.
**5. Voltages:** phase voltage U_A = √(220² + 40²) = **223.6 V**; in the line voltage u_AB = u_A − u_B the 3rd harmonics cancel, U_AB = √3 × 220 = **381.1 V**, so U_AB < √3U_A = 387.3 V.
**Check:** for the 3rd harmonic the neutral current is a single-phase loop: the three loads in parallel, Z_3/3, across 40 V: 40/(25/3) = 4.8 A — the same.

questions.explain: u_AB = u_A − u_B: the fundamentals give √3 × 220 = 381.1 V; the 3rd harmonics are in phase and cancel. So U_AB = 381.1 V, **not** √3 × 223.6 = 387.3 V.

questions.ask: rms current of phase A, I_A = ?
Reading of the neutral ammeter, I_N = ?
questions.explain: The fundamental currents are balanced and add up to zero in the neutral; the 3rd-harmonic currents are in phase and add up to 3I_A3 = 4.8 A.

questions.ask: What goes wrong if you multiply the rms phase voltage by √3 to get the line voltage?
choices: Too large: the 3rd harmonics cancel in the line voltage, so √3 does not apply
Too small: it misses √3 times the 3rd harmonic
Nothing: the line voltage is always √3 times the phase voltage
Too large: the fundamentals cancel in the line voltage
choiceExplain: In the line voltage the 3rd harmonics **subtract** to zero; they are not multiplied by √3.
U_l = √3U_p holds only for a balanced positive- (or negative-) sequence set; the zero-sequence 3rd harmonic does not obey it.
What cancels is the in-phase 3rd harmonic, not the fundamentals that are 120° apart.
questions.explain: √3 × 223.6 = 387.3 V > 381.1 V. Only the fundamental (and the 5th, 7th, … harmonics that are not multiples of 3) obey the √3 relation; harmonics that are multiples of 3 vanish from the line voltage.
